questions.text:
In a pushdown automaton [latex]P=(Q, \Sigma, \Gamma, \delta, q_0, F)[/latex], a transition of the form,

where [latex]p,q \in Q \; a \in \sigma \cup \{ \epsilon \} ,\;X,Y, \in \Gamma \cup \{ \epsilon \}[/latex], represents

[latex](q,Y) \in \delta(p,a,X)[/latex]

Consider the following pushdown automaton over the input alphabet [latex]\Sigma = \{a,b\}[/latex] and stack alphabet [latex]\Gamma = \{ \#, A\}[/latex].

The number of strings of length 100 accepted by the above pushdown automaton is ___________
questions.solution:
The PDA pushes # and then an A for every a; in q2 every b pops an A. It can reach the final state q3 only if an A is still on top.

So it accepts [latex]a^mb^n[/latex] with [latex]n \lt m[/latex]. For length 100: m + n = 100 with n [latex]\lt[/latex] m [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] n = 0, 1, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 49 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 50 strings.

Answer: 50

questions.text:
Consider the following matrix.
[latex]\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\\ 1& 0& 1 & 1\\ 1& 1 & 0 & 1 \\1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}[/latex]
The largest eigenvalue of the above matrix is __________.
questions.solution:
The matrix is [latex]J-I[/latex], where J is the 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 all-ones matrix.
Eigenvalues of J: 4, 0, 0, 0. Subtracting 1: 3, [latex]-[/latex]1, [latex]-[/latex]1, [latex]-[/latex]1.

Largest = 3

Answer: 3

questions.text:
A five-stage pipeline has stage delays of 150, 120, 150, 160 and 140 nanoseconds. The registers that are used between the pipeline stages have a delay of 5 nanoseconds each.
The total time to execute 100 independent instructions on this pipeline, assuming there are no pipeline stalls, is _______ nanoseconds.
questions.solution:
Clock cycle = slowest stage + register delay = 160 + 5 = 165 ns.
Cycles for 100 instructions on 5 stages = 5 + 100 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 104.

Time = 104 [latex]\times[/latex] 165 = 17160 ns

Answer: 17160

questions.text:
A sender (S) transmits a signal, which can be one of the two kinds: H and L with probabilities 0.1 and 0.9 respectively, to a receiver (R)
In the graph below, the weight of edge [latex](u,v)[/latex] is the probability of receiving [latex]v[/latex] when [latex]u[/latex] is transmitted, where [latex]u,v\in\{H,L\}[/latex]. For example, the probability that the received signal is [latex]L[/latex] given the transmitted signal was [latex]H[/latex], is 0.7.

If the received signal is [latex]H[/latex], the probability that the transmitted signal was [latex]H[/latex] (rounded to 2 decimal places) is __________.
questions.solution:
From the graph: P(recv H | sent H) = 0.3 and P(recv H | sent L) = 0.8.

P(recv H) = 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.3 + 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.8 = 0.03 + 0.72 = 0.75

Bayes: [latex]P(\text{sent H}\mid\text{recv H})=\frac{0.03}{0.75}=0.04[/latex]

Answer: 0.04

questions.text:
Consider the following instruction sequence where registers [latex]R_1,R_2 \text{ and }R_3[/latex] are general purpose and [latex]MEMORY[X][/latex] denotes the content at the memory location [latex]X[/latex].

[latex]\begin{array}{llc} \textbf{Instruction} & \textbf{Semantics} & \textbf{Instruction Size} \text{ (bytes)} \\ \hline \text{MOV } R1, (5000) & R1 \leftarrow \text{MEMORY}[5000] & 4 \\ \hline \text{MOV } R2, (R3) & R2 \leftarrow \text{MEMORY}[R3] & 4 \\ \hline \text{ADD} R2, R1 & R2 \leftarrow R1 + R2 & 2 \\ \hline \text{MOV } (R3), R2 & \text{MEMORY}[R3] \leftarrow R2 & 4 \\ \hline \text{INC } R3 & R3 \leftarrow R3+1 & 2 \\ \hline \text{DEC } R1 & R1 \leftarrow R1-1 & 2 \\ \hline \text{BNZ } 1004 & \text{Branch if not zero to the} & 2 \\ & \text{given absolute address} \\ \hline \text{HALT} & \text{Stop} & 1 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]

Assume that the content of the memory location 5000 is 10, and the content of the register [latex]R_3[/latex] is 3000. The content of each of the memory locations from 3000 to 3020 is 50. The instruction sequence starts from the memory location 1000. All the numbers are in decimal format. Assume that the memory is byte addressable.
After the execution of the program, the content of memory location 3010 is ____________
questions.solution:
R1 = MEMORY[5000] = 10, so the loop (BNZ back to 1004) runs 10 times. Each pass adds R1 to MEMORY[R3] and moves R3 one byte ahead.

R3 goes 3000, 3001, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 3009. Location 3010 is never written, so it keeps its value 50.

Answer: 50
